title: The Class of Heroes
tagline: data that knows how to look after itself
hints: A class body is `class Hero { public: ... private: ... };` - semicolon after the closing brace, exactly like a struct.
The constructor has the same name as the class and no return type: `Hero(std::string name, int maxHp) { ... }`. It runs when the object is made.
Trailing underscores (`hp_`, `name_`) are a common way to tell a member apart from a parameter with the same meaning. Nothing magic - just a habit that saves confusion.
`bool isAlive() const` - the `const` after the parentheses promises this method changes nothing. Put it on every method that only reads, and the compiler will catch you if you lie.
`status()` builds a string rather than printing one. Use `std::to_string(hp_)` to turn a number into text, and `+` to glue pieces together.
